entries.clue: Perhaps Marilyn's sweetheart to take care of a little rusty instrument (6,4)

indicators.note: only a little of the word, its first letter
the sweetheart looks after R by holding it inside

blocks.note: Marilyn French, the American novelist; 'perhaps' marks her as one example of a French
hon, short for honey, a term of endearment
a little of rusty: its first letter

annotation.surface: Marilyn's lover is asked to look after an old, somewhat rusty instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marilyn' pulls towards Monroe, but the setter wants a surname: Marilyn French wrote The Women's Room. The 's stands for 'has', joining her to the sweetheart.
annotation.definitionFit: The French horn is a brass instrument with a coiled tube and a wide flared bell.

entries.clue: Foundered when afield, reeling (6)

indicators.note: staggering about, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Someone out in the fields staggers and comes to grief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foundered' looks like it wants a shipwreck word, but here it simply means came to nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plan that foundered collapsed, which is to say it failed.

entries.clue: Relax: that man's not still in bed, Cockney informs us (4,2)

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the H at the start of words, so he's becomes 'e's
tells us out loud, so we go by sound

blocks.clueFragment: that man's not still in bed
blocks.note: he's up, said with the Cockney dropped H

annotation.surface: A Cockney reports that the man of the house is finally out of bed, so everyone can relax.
annotation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, whose accent famously drops the H: he's up comes out as 'e's up, identical to EASE UP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: easing up on something means slackening, which is how one relaxes.

entries.clue: Inventor: Bach and Elgar's confused with Barber – runs off (7,7)

indicators.note: the composers' names are jumbled together
the runs are taken away before the jumbling

blocks.note: the composer, as printed
the composer, S included
Samuel Barber, the composer, as printed
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run; runs, plural, removes two Rs

annotation.surface: Three composers are muddled up, and the orchestra's scores go missing.
annotation.walkthrough: Remove the two Rs from BACHELGARSBARBER, then rearrange. The clue reads like a concert programme; Babbage designed the Difference Engine, a mechanical computer.
annotation.definitionFit: Charles Babbage was the Victorian inventor of the Difference and Analytical Engines, forerunners of the computer.

entries.clue: Hullabaloo near duchy that's neglected (3,3,3)

indicators.note: left uncared for, and so in disarray

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: Uproar breaks out close to a ducal estate that has been left to rot.
annotation.walkthrough: A duchy is a territory ruled by a duke; it is only letters here.
annotation.definitionFit: A hue and cry is a loud public outcry, a hullabaloo.

entries.clue: Lead operations, in charge of mysterious characters (5)

annotation.definitionNote: RUNIC is an adjective; read the definition as 'of mysterious characters', written in runes

blocks.note: to run a business is to lead its operations
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

annotation.surface: A manager is put in charge of operations involving some cryptic symbols.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In charge of' reads as one phrase, but 'of' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Runic means written in runes, the old Germanic alphabet, and so by extension mysterious.

entries.clue: Betrayer turned, protecting second despot (4)

indicators.note: the betrayer is turned round, read backwards
the turned word surrounds S, shielding it

blocks.note: a rat is someone who betrays their friends
S is the standard abbreviation for second

annotation.surface: A traitor switches sides and ends up guarding the tyrant's number two.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned' suggests a turncoat, which suits a betrayer, but it is an instruction to read RAT backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A tsar was the absolute ruler of Russia, a byword for a despot.

entries.clue: Sensible to get to grips with bit of progress that's cutting-edge (5-3)

indicators.note: the sensible word grips the other, holding it inside

blocks.note: sage means wise, sensible
a pace is a single step, a bit of forward movement

annotation.surface: A level-headed person tackles a small step forward in the latest technology.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit of progress' looks like it wants a letter taken from progress, but it is a whole word: a pace.
annotation.definitionFit: Space-age means ultra-modern, futuristic, at the cutting edge.

entries.clue: Sympathise with concern (6,2)

blocks.note: to feel for someone, identify with their situation
a verb here: to have a bearing on, be about

annotation.surface: Someone is told to share another's worry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Concern' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: this matter concerns you, relates to you.
annotation.definitionFit: Two separate senses of one phrasal verb: feeling a bond with someone, and having a bearing on a matter.

entries.clue: Gorges on English seafood, right away, with most of roll and vegetable (7,7)

indicators.note: R, right, goes away from the seafood
all but the last letter of the roll

blocks.note: a chine is a deep narrow ravine, a gorge
E is the standard abbreviation for English
CRAB with R, right, removed
BAGEL, a bread roll, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone gorges on English crab, then most of a bread roll and some greens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gorges' reads as a verb for overeating, which suits the menu, but it is the noun: chines are ravines, a word most familiar from the Isle of Wight.
annotation.definitionFit: Chinese cabbage, such as pak choi or napa cabbage, is a leafy vegetable.

entries.clue: Enthrone in rumpled satinet (7)

indicators.note: crumpled, so the letters are messed up

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A monarch is crowned in creased satin-like cloth.
annotation.walkthrough: Satinet is a thin imitation satin; the unusual word is chosen for its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: To instate someone is to install them in office, as enthroning installs a monarch.

entries.clue: Native Americans handing us 'avocado', 'tomato', linguistically (primarily)? (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: the first letters of the seven words

annotation.surface: A note that native American peoples gave us the words avocado and tomato.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Nahuatl, the Aztec language of Mexico, is where English got avocado and tomato.
annotation.definitionFit: Nahuatl is the language of the Aztecs, still spoken in Mexico, the source of avocado, tomato and chocolate.

entries.clue: Some prequalify in uniform (5)

indicators.note: only part of the next word is needed

blocks.note: the letters sit inside, after PR and before IFY

annotation.surface: Some candidates prequalify while in uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like the noun, clothing, but it is the adjective: all the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Things that are uniform are all equal, the same throughout.

entries.clue: Rain's stopped play? It's a foregone conclusion (2,7)

blocks.note: read literally: when rain halts play, no match takes place
a result so certain the match is not worth playing

annotation.surface: Rain halts a cricket match, and everyone knew how it would end anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the first definition as a playful literal reading: a match called off for rain means no contest took place.
annotation.definitionFit: A no-contest is a match so one-sided the result is a foregone conclusion.

entries.clue: A witch may have this assistant, bit of a fright (6,5)

blocks.note: a second is an assistant, as in a duel or boxing
someone who looks a fright looks a sight

annotation.surface: A witch's helper gives people a bit of a scare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Assistant' seems to continue the witch's story, as a familiar, but it is a boxer's second. 'You look a sight' means you look a fright.
annotation.definitionFit: Second sight is the power to see the future, the kind of gift a witch is credited with.

entries.clue: Attests to the bona fides of suspicious señoritas (9)

annotation.definition: Attests to the bona fides of

indicators.note: dubious, not in their proper order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange, the tilde ignored

annotation.surface: An official vouches for some young Spanish women whom others regard with suspicion.
annotation.walkthrough: Señoritas are young unmarried Spanish women; only their letters are wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: A notary notarises a document, formally certifying that it and its signatures are genuine.

entries.clue: Tape in difficult test case (8)

indicators.note: awkward, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

annotation.surface: A recording turns up as evidence in a hard legal test case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Difficult test case' reads as legal jargon, but 'difficult' is the only instruction here.
annotation.definitionFit: Tape here means a recording on magnetic tape, and the cassette is the plastic case that holds one.

entries.clue: This answer may be saline (8)

blocks.note: the clue refers to itself: what the solver writes in
saline is salt dissolved in water, one example of a liquid mixture of that kind

annotation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: 'This answer' is the solution. Saline is one example of a solution, hence 'may be'.
annotation.definitionFit: A solution is both an answer to a puzzle and a liquid with something dissolved in it, such as saline.

entries.clue: Destructive policy: a pact must be arranged (11)

indicators.note: the letters have to be put into a new order

blocks.note: part of the letters to rearrange
the rest of the letters

annotation.surface: A ruinous policy leads to the conclusion that a treaty has to be drawn up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Policy' reads as part of the definition, but only 'Destructive' defines; the colon separates it.
annotation.definitionFit: Apocalyptic means catastrophically destructive, like the end of the world.

entries.clue: Make new arrangement for holidaymaker's destination (6)

blocks.note: to sort again, with a hyphen-free prefix RE-
a place such as a seaside town that holidaymakers head for

annotation.surface: A travel agent rebooks a tourist's trip.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is RE-SORT, sort again, spelt the same as the holiday word.
annotation.definitionFit: To re-sort is to arrange again; a resort is where holidaymakers go.

entries.clue: For model: cheers! (6)

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
to sit for an artist is to model

annotation.surface: A toast raised to a model.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For model' reads as for the benefit of a model, but each word is a separate piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Prosit is a Latin-derived toast, used in German, meaning 'may it benefit you': cheers!

entries.clue: Small woodsman, one that's out for a bit (9)

annotation.definition: one that's out for a bit

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
a lumberer fells and cuts timber

annotation.surface: A little lumberjack steps outside for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out for a bit' sounds like popping outdoors, but it means asleep, out cold for a while.
annotation.definitionFit: Being out for a bit is slang for a short sleep, and one who sleeps is a slumberer.

entries.clue: Set of pulses directed one way ... or another (5)

indicators.note: the word reads the same in one direction or the other

blocks.note: a word that reads the same either way

annotation.surface: Pulses are aimed first this way, then that.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One way ... or another' sounds like it describes the sweep of the pulses, but it says the word reads identically in both directions.
annotation.definitionFit: Radar works by sending out directed radio pulses and timing their echoes.

entries.clue: Dim British king (5)

blocks.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
King Lear, Shakespeare's king

annotation.surface: A slow-witted British monarch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dim' looks like it means stupid, fitting a king, but it means blurred.
annotation.definitionFit: Blear means dim or blurred, as bleary eyes see things.

entries.clue: Medically assessed the 'riddle' at the outset: Everyman's got old (7)

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so only the start of each word, its first letter, is kept

blocks.note: the first letters of the and riddle
the setter, Everyman, refers to himself as I
aged means old

annotation.surface: The setter admits he has grown old puzzling over a riddle.
annotation.walkthrough: A setter naming himself stands for I, me. 'The' looks like filler but supplies the T.
annotation.definitionFit: Casualties are triaged when medically assessed to decide who is treated first.

entries.clue: Adds quality to multiple TV episodes (7)

blocks.note: seasoning food improves its flavour
a TV series is sold in yearly runs of episodes; plural

annotation.surface: A long-running show gets better over time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Multiple' is there to make the second definition plural, matching SEASONS.
annotation.definitionFit: A cook seasons food to improve its flavour; a TV series comes in seasons.

entries.clue: Woman essential to United Nations (4)

indicators.note: found in the very core of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters straddle the break, the end of United and the start of Nations

annotation.surface: A woman is indispensable to the UN.
annotation.walkthrough: Crosswords often define a first name simply as 'woman' or 'girl'.
annotation.definitionFit: Crosswords use 'woman' to define any female first name, and Edna is one.

entries.clue: Spooner's assessed judgment, briefly seeing bird (7,3)

indicators.note: Rev Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words
judgment is shortened to CRIT

blocks.note: assessed = tested, which gives up its T and takes the CR from the next word
crit is short for critique, a judgment; it hands over its CR and takes the T

annotation.surface: Someone's hasty verdict on what they have assessed involves spotting a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of TESTED and CRIT to get CRESTED TIT. A crit is a critique, the short form familiar from art schools.
annotation.definitionFit: The crested tit is a small European songbird with a pointed crest.
